title: Coefficient conversion preserves the extension-by-zero counit
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the inclusion of an open subscheme. Let $A$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Let $E:\mathrm{Ab}\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathrm{ULift}\,\mathbf Z)$ be the inverse of the forgetful equivalence from integer modules followed by restriction of scalars along the ring isomorphism $\mathrm{ULift}\,\mathbf Z\simeq\mathbf Z$. Write $T_X$ for objectwise composition with $E$ on sheaves. Using inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] in the respective coefficient categories, there exists an isomorphism
$$e:j_!j^*(T_X A)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X(j_!j^*A)$$
with
$$e\,;\,T_X(\epsilon_A)=\epsilon_{T_X A},$$
where both arrows $\epsilon$ are the counits of the extension-by-zero adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. No density or curve hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), counit arrow; Tag 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), conversion to module coefficients in the application

proof.text: The integer-module forgetful equivalence and restriction along the ring isomorphism give the coefficient equivalence E. Its inverse, unit and counit applied objectwise give equivalences of the sheaf categories: equivalences preserve the limits defining the sheaf condition.

The module inverse-image/underlying-abelian-sheaf compatibility, together with the coefficient equivalence unit and counit, identifies module inverse image of T_X A with T_U of abelian inverse image. For the open immersion this can also be seen directly by upperStarIsoOpenImmersionRestriction: restriction is precomposition, which commutes with coefficient composition.

Transport the abelian extension-by-zero adjunction through these coefficient equivalences. Its right adjoint is identified with module inverse image, so uniqueness of left adjoints supplies the isomorphism e with module extension by zero. The counit compatibility of the canonical leftAdjointUniq isomorphism yields e.hom followed by T_X of the abelian counit equal to the module counit. This specifies the isomorphism rather than asserting compatibility for an arbitrary isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Categorical expansion of the coefficient convention for the counit in 095L and 0GJA; uniqueness and counit compatibility of left adjoints

theorem exists_lowerShriek_coefficient_counit {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (U : X.Opens) (A : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    let E := (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} ℤ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).inv ⋙
      ModuleCat.restrictScalars (ULift.ringEquiv : ULift.{u + 1} ℤ ≃+* ℤ).toRingHom
    let T := sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology E
    ∃ e : (openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)) U.ι).obj
        ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)) U.ι).obj (T.obj A)) ≅
      T.obj ((openImmersionLowerShriek AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U.ι).obj
        ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U.ι).obj A)),
      e.hom ≫ T.map
          ((openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U.ι).counit.app A)
        = (openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)) U.ι).counit.app (T.obj A)
